title: Vertical Oscillation
claims: Garmin defines vertical oscillation as the amount of bounce in each step, measured at the torso in centimetres.
Garmin states that more experienced runners tend to have lower vertical oscillation, but that faster paces often come at the cost of somewhat higher vertical oscillation.
Garmin states that lower vertical oscillation typically means less stress on the lower body at impact.
Garmin's page gives no normal range and no threshold value for vertical oscillation.
